name: Robert Rubin

summary.text: Robert E. Rubin was U.S. Secretary of the Treasury from 1995 to 1999, succeeding Lloyd Bentsen, after twenty-six years at Goldman Sachs where he rose to co-chairman. The Treasury's official history says he led efforts with the IMF, the Federal Reserve and others to keep the Mexican and Asian financial crises from overwhelming the global financial system. In 1999 he joined Citigroup as chairman of its executive committee and later sat on its board; he was called before the Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission in 2010.

sources.title: Rubin, Greenspan, Prince to be Grilled by Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission

facts.claim: Rubin succeeded Lloyd Bentsen as Treasury Secretary in 1995 and served until 1999; the Treasury's history says he faced financial crises in Mexico and Asia that posed real risks to global financial stability and led efforts with the IMF, the Federal Reserve and others to stop them from overwhelming the global financial system.
Before government service Rubin worked for twenty-six years at Goldman Sachs, rising to co-chairman.

facts.claim: In 1999 Rubin joined Citigroup as chairman of its executive committee and later served as a board member.

openQuestions: Site description 'U.S. Treasury Secretary who pushed for tough IMF conditionality and market-opening terms': his leading role with the IMF is documented by Treasury's history; the characterisation of the terms as 'tough' comes from critics (CEPR, Weisbrot) rather than from an official record.
Site claims about the closure of 56 Thai finance companies and 16 Indonesian banks and about Carlyle, Newbridge and Lone Star acquisitions were not tested here.
